chunks: For the petitioner (one who asks) and the dispossessed (one who is deprived).

key_terms.السَّائِلِ: The petitioner; one who asks for charity or aid.
key_terms.الْمَحْرُومِ: The dispossessed; one who is deprived of wealth or status.

ai.seo_question: Who are the sa'il and mahroom in Islamic social welfare?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this pairing underscores the dual nature of social justice by addressing both the active claimant (as-sa'il) and the structurally marginalized (al-mahroom), reflecting the concept of *haqq al-mustahiqqin* (right of the deserving). This distinction is pivotal in understanding the distribution of *zakat* and *khums*, ensuring that aid reaches not only those who ask but also those too deprived to seek it, thereby fulfilling the comprehensive welfare mandate of the Imams.
